subproblem.title: Images of open sets under C¹ maps ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q are countably n-rectifiable
subproblem.statement: For all Q, n ∈ ℕ, every map G : ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q and every open O ⊆ ℝⁿ such that G is C¹ on O, the image G(O) is countably n-rectifiable.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (Q n : ℕ) (G : Eucl n → Eucl Q) (O : Set (Eucl n)), IsOpen O → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 G O → CountablyRectifiable n (G '' O)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions: ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) (Lean `Eucl P`); ℝⁿ = `Eucl n`. An n-covector on E is a continuous alternating n-linear map α : Eⁿ → ℝ (`Covector E n` = `E [⋀^Fin n]→L[ℝ] ℝ`, a real vector space under pointwise operations). Countably n-rectifiable (`CountablyRectifiable n S`, SimonGMT Ch. 3, Def. 1.1) means: there are an Hⁿ-null set S₀ and Lipschitz maps F_j : ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q (j ∈ ℕ) with S ⊆ S₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝⁿ). The child proof is written in a file whose imports are fixed (`import GMT.Ch06.Submission`); every result cited below is available there.

This is the fact, used in Step 11 (countablyRectifiable) of the parent proof, that each chart image G_k(O_k) is countably n-rectifiable. It is the argument of SimonGMT's `countablyRectifiable_image_contDiffOn_open` (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.SubmanifoldCover), reproduced here because that module is not imported by GMT.Ch06.Submission and a child may not add imports.

1. (Compact exhaustion of O.) O is an open subset of the locally compact, σ-compact space ℝⁿ, so the subspace O is locally compact (`IsOpen.locallyCompactSpace`) and σ-compact. Hence there are compact sets K_j of the subspace O (j ∈ ℕ) covering O (`SigmaCompactSpace.exists_compact_covering`). Their images C_j ⊆ ℝⁿ under the inclusion O → ℝⁿ are compact (continuous image), satisfy C_j ⊆ O, and ⋃_j C_j = O.
2. (G is Lipschitz on each C_j.) Let x ∈ C_j ⊆ O. Since O is open and G is C¹ on O, G is C¹ at x (`ContDiffOn.contDiffAt` with O ∈ 𝓝 x), hence Lipschitz on some neighbourhood t_x of x with some constant (`ContDiffAt.exists_lipschitzOnWith`). So G is locally Lipschitz on C_j, and since C_j is compact, G is L_j-Lipschitz on all of C_j for some L_j ≥ 0 (`LocallyLipschitzOn.exists_lipschitzOnWith_of_compact`).
3. (Lipschitz extension.) A Lipschitz map from a subset of ℝⁿ into the finite-dimensional normed space ℝ^Q extends to a Lipschitz map on all of ℝⁿ (`LipschitzOnWith.extend_finite_dimension`): there is a Lipschitz g_j : ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q with g_j = G on C_j.
4. (Rectifiability.) The range of a single Lipschitz map ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q is countably n-rectifiable (take S₀ = ∅ and F_i = g_j for all i; `Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.countablyRectifiable_range`). A countable union of countably n-rectifiable sets is countably n-rectifiable (`Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.countablyRectifiable_iUnion`), and so is every subset of a countably n-rectifiable set (`CountablyRectifiable.mono`). Hence ⋃_j g_j(ℝⁿ) is countably n-rectifiable.
5. (Inclusion.) Let y ∈ G(O), y = G(x) with x ∈ O. By Step 1, x ∈ C_j for some j, and by Step 3, y = G(x) = g_j(x) ∈ g_j(ℝⁿ). Thus G(O) ⊆ ⋃_j g_j(ℝⁿ), and G(O) is countably n-rectifiable by Step 4. ∎

subproblem.title: Finite-dimensionality of the space of n-covectors on ℝ^Q
subproblem.statement: For all Q, n ∈ ℕ, the real vector space Covector(ℝ^Q, n) of continuous alternating n-linear maps (ℝ^Q)ⁿ → ℝ is finite-dimensional.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (Q n : ℕ), FiniteDimensional ℝ (Covector (Eucl Q) n)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions: ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) (Lean `Eucl P`); ℝⁿ = `Eucl n`. An n-covector on E is a continuous alternating n-linear map α : Eⁿ → ℝ (`Covector E n` = `E [⋀^Fin n]→L[ℝ] ℝ`, a real vector space under pointwise operations). Countably n-rectifiable (`CountablyRectifiable n S`, SimonGMT Ch. 3, Def. 1.1) means: there are an Hⁿ-null set S₀ and Lipschitz maps F_j : ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q (j ∈ ℕ) with S ⊆ S₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝⁿ). The child proof is written in a file whose imports are fixed (`import GMT.Ch06.Submission`); every result cited below is available there.

This is the finite-dimensionality of the space of n-covectors used for the measurability of the image density in Step 8 of the parent proof (there via a basis β_1,…,β_N of n-covectors). It is proved by embedding Covector(ℝ^Q, n) linearly and injectively into a finite-dimensional coordinate space.

1. Let e_1,…,e_Q be the standard basis of ℝ^Q (e_j = `EuclideanSpace.single j 1`). Define F : Covector(ℝ^Q, n) → ℝ^{(Fin n → Fin Q)} by F(α)(r) := α(e_{r(1)}, …, e_{r(n)}) for every map r : Fin n → Fin Q. Evaluation of α at a fixed n-tuple is linear in α, so F is linear.
2. (F is injective.) Let a, b be n-covectors with F(a) = F(b), and let v = (v_1,…,v_n) ∈ (ℝ^Q)ⁿ. Each v_i = Σ_j v_i(j) e_j (expansion in the standard orthonormal basis, `EuclideanSpace.basisFun` with `OrthonormalBasis.sum_repr`). For any n-covector c, multilinearity (`MultilinearMap.map_sum` applied to c.toMultilinearMap) gives c(v) = Σ_{r : Fin n → Fin Q} c(i ↦ v_i(r(i)) • e_{r(i)}), and pulling the scalars out of each slot (`map_smul_univ`) gives c(i ↦ v_i(r(i)) • e_{r(i)}) = (Π_i v_i(r(i))) · c(i ↦ e_{r(i)}) = (Π_i v_i(r(i))) · F(c)(r). Applying this to c = a and c = b and using F(a)(r) = F(b)(r) for every r gives a(v) = b(v). As v was arbitrary, a = b (extensionality of continuous alternating maps).
3. The codomain ℝ^{(Fin n → Fin Q)} consists of real functions on a finite type, so it is finite-dimensional. A real vector space that admits an injective linear map into a finite-dimensional space is finite-dimensional (`Module.Finite.of_injective`; the codomain is a Noetherian ℝ-module, being finite-dimensional over the field ℝ). Hence Covector(ℝ^Q, n) is finite-dimensional. (The degenerate cases need no separate treatment: for n = 0 the index type Fin 0 → Fin Q has one element and F(α) records α(∅); for Q = 0 and n ≥ 1 both sides vanish.) ∎

1. Put h⁺(x) := ofReal(g(x)) and h⁻(x) := ofReal(−g(x)). Both are μ⌞A-a.e. measurable (g is). Pointwise h⁺ + h⁻ = ‖g‖ₑ (ofReal(a) + ofReal(−a) = |a| for a ∈ ℝ), and g = (h⁺).toReal − (h⁻).toReal.
2. By the area identity, N⁺ := N^{h⁺} and N⁻ := N^{h⁻} are ν-a.e. measurable and ∫⁻ N^± dν = ∫⁻_A h^± J dμ. Each is ≤ ∫⁻_A ‖g‖ₑ J dμ < ∞, because h^± ≤ ‖g‖ₑ. An a.e. measurable [0, ∞]-valued function with finite lintegral is a.e. finite (`ae_lt_top'`), so N⁺ < ∞ and N⁻ < ∞ ν-a.e.
3. Fix y with N⁺(y) < ∞ and N⁻(y) < ∞. The fibre sum of ‖g‖ₑ equals N⁺(y) + N⁻(y) < ∞ (`ENNReal.tsum_add`). So the nonnegative real family ‖g(x)‖ is summable (`ENNReal.tsum_coe_ne_top_iff_summable` for ‖g‖₊), and therefore (g(x))_x is summable in the complete space ℝ (`Summable.of_norm`). This proves (i). The families max(g, 0) = (h⁺).toReal and max(−g, 0) = (h⁻).toReal are dominated by ‖g‖, hence also summable, with sums N⁺(y).toReal and N⁻(y).toReal (`ENNReal.tsum_toReal_eq` with finiteness). Since g = (h⁺).toReal − (h⁻).toReal termwise, Σ'_x g(x) = N⁺(y).toReal − N⁻(y).toReal.
4. The functions y ↦ N^±(y).toReal are ν-a.e. measurable and nonnegative with ∫⁻ ofReal(N^±.toReal) ≤ ∫⁻ N^± < ∞, so they are ν-integrable. By `integral_toReal` (using N^± < ∞ a.e.), ∫ N^±(y).toReal dν = (∫⁻ N^± dν).toReal. By Step 3, y ↦ Σ'_x g(x) agrees ν-a.e. with N⁺.toReal − N⁻.toReal. Hence it is ν-integrable (proving (ii)) and ∫ Σ' g dν = (∫⁻_A h⁺ J dμ).toReal − (∫⁻_A h⁻ J dμ).toReal.
5. On the source side, ∫⁻_A ‖g‖ₑ J < ∞ forces ‖g‖ₑ J < ∞ μ⌞A-a.e. Hence g(x) = 0 for μ⌞A-a.e. x with J(x) = ∞. Consequently, μ⌞A-a.e., ofReal(g·J.toReal) = h⁺·J and ofReal(−g·J.toReal) = h⁻·J. Where J < ∞ this is ofReal(ab) = ofReal(a)·ofReal(b) for b = J.toReal ≥ 0, with ofReal(J.toReal) = J; where J = ∞ both sides are 0 because g = 0.
6. The real function g·J.toReal is μ⌞A-a.e. strongly measurable (g a.e. strongly measurable, J a.e. measurable). Its lintegral of absolute values satisfies ∫⁻_A ‖g·J.toReal‖ₑ ≤ ∫⁻_A ‖g‖ₑ J < ∞, so it is μ⌞A-integrable. By the positive/negative-part formula for the Bochner integral (`integral_eq_lintegral_pos_part_sub_lintegral_neg_part`) and Step 5, ∫_A g·J.toReal dμ = (∫⁻_A h⁺ J).toReal − (∫⁻_A h⁻ J).toReal.
7. Steps 4 and 6 have the same right-hand side, which gives (iii). ∎

An n-covector on E is a continuous alternating n-linear map α : Eⁿ → ℝ with the operator norm. An n-vector is a continuous linear functional on n-covectors (`NVector E n`), also with the operator norm. simpleNVector v is the n-vector α ↦ α(v₁,…,vₙ). For a continuous linear map A, A_#u := nVectorPushforward n A u = u ∘ A^#, where A^#α = α(A·,…,A·). Thus A_# is linear in u, and A_#(simpleNVector v) = simpleNVector(A∘v) (`nVectorPushforward_simple`). `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x T` is Simon's weighted approximate tangent space (Ch. 3, 1.7). By SimonGMT `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique` it is unique when θ(x) ≠ 0, and its first component says dim T = n. The derivative clause for (M, θ, f, L) means: for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x, for every subspace T with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x T and every v ∈ T, the map t ↦ f(x + t v) has derivative L(x)v at t = 0. Φ is c-antilipschitz on Ω if c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω.

This lemma packages the linear algebra used in Steps 3 and 8 of the parent proof: unit simple n-vectors orienting the same plane differ by a sign. It is proved from (SNA) as follows.

1. (a) Let σ : Fin n → ℝ^Q be orthonormal. Then ⟨σ_i, σ_j⟩ = 1 if i = j and 0 otherwise, so the Gram matrix (⟨σ_i, σ_j⟩)_{i,j} is the identity matrix I_n. Its determinant is 1; for n = 0 the empty matrix also has determinant 1. By the first conjunct of (SNA), ‖simpleNVector σ‖² = det I_n = 1. A norm is ≥ 0, so ‖simpleNVector σ‖ = 1.
2. (b) Let σ, σ′ be orthonormal with span(range σ) = span(range σ′). For each i, σ′_i ∈ span(range σ′) = span(range σ). An element of the span of the finite family σ is a linear combination of it (`Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun`), so there are reals B_i1,…,B_in with σ′_i = Σ_j B_ij σ_j. Let B := (B_ij) ∈ ℝ^{n×n}. Then σ′ = (i ↦ Σ_j B_ij • σ_j) as functions Fin n → ℝ^Q (funext).
3. By the second conjunct of (SNA), simpleNVector σ′ = det(B) • simpleNVector σ.
4. Take norms and apply Step 1 to both σ and σ′: 1 = ‖simpleNVector σ′‖ = |det B|·‖simpleNVector σ‖ = |det B|. Hence det B = 1 or det B = −1.
5. If det B = 1, Step 3 gives simpleNVector σ′ = simpleNVector σ. If det B = −1, it gives simpleNVector σ′ = (−1) • simpleNVector σ = −simpleNVector σ. ∎

Conventions: ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) (Lean `Eucl P`) with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|; Hⁿ = μHE[n], Mathlib's Euclidean-normalised n-dimensional Hausdorff measure, which equals Lebesgue measure Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ. An n-covector on E is a continuous alternating n-linear map α : Eⁿ → ℝ with the operator norm. An n-vector is a continuous linear functional on n-covectors (`NVector E n`), also with the operator norm. simpleNVector v is the n-vector α ↦ α(v₁,…,vₙ). For a continuous linear map A, A_#u := nVectorPushforward n A u = u ∘ A^#, where A^#α = α(A·,…,A·). Thus A_# is linear in u, and A_#(simpleNVector v) = simpleNVector(A∘v) (`nVectorPushforward_simple`). `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x T` is Simon's weighted approximate tangent space (Ch. 3, 1.7). By SimonGMT `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique` it is unique when θ(x) ≠ 0, and its first component says dim T = n. The derivative clause for (M, θ, f, L) means: for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x, for every subspace T with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x T and every v ∈ T, the map t ↦ f(x + t v) has derivative L(x)v at t = 0. Φ is c-antilipschitz on Ω if c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω.

1. (Tangent planes of (Y, 1).) For each k apply (WTC) to (V, Y, θ ≡ 1, G_k, O_k). The hypotheses hold: V open; Y ⊆ V null-measurable; 1 > 0; 1 is integrable on Y ∩ K because Hⁿ(Y ∩ K) < ∞ (`integrableOn_const_iff`); O_k open; G_k C¹ and antilipschitz. Let E_k be the set of y ∈ Y ∩ G_k(O_k) for which some w ∈ O_k with G_k(w) = y fails HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n Y 1 y (range DG_k(w)). E_k is Hⁿ-null because μ(t ∩ s) ≤ μ⌞s(t) (`Measure.le_restrict_apply`). Let E₀ be the set of y ∈ Y for which the assumed family does not exist; Hⁿ(E₀) = 0, again because μ(t ∩ s) ≤ μ⌞s(t) (`Measure.le_restrict_apply`), here with s = Y. Put E := E₀ ∪ ⋃_k E_k, an Hⁿ-null set.
2. (Common plane, integer coefficient.) Let y ∈ Y ∖ E with family (m, a, k, w, σ) and m ≥ 1. For each i, y = G_{k_i}(w_i) ∈ Y ∩ G_{k_i}(O_{k_i}) and y ∉ E_{k_i}, so HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n Y 1 y (span(range σ_i)). The weight 1 is nonzero, so uniqueness (`HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique`) gives span(range σ_i) = span(range σ_1) for every i. By part (b) of the sibling lemma lpf_pi_simple_unit_facts (applied to (SNA)), simpleNVector σ_i = ε_i • simpleNVector σ_1 with ε_i ∈ {1, −1}. Hence Ψ(y) = c(y) • simpleNVector σ_1 with c(y) := Σ_i ε_i a_i ∈ ℤ. By part (a) of lpf_pi_simple_unit_facts, ‖Ψ(y)‖ = |c(y)|. If m = 0, then Ψ(y) = 0 (empty sum).
3. (The new triple.) Put M′ := {y ∈ Y ∖ E : Ψ(y) ≠ 0}, θ′(y) := ‖Ψ(y)‖ and ξ′(y) := ‖Ψ(y)‖⁻¹ • Ψ(y). For y ∈ M′, Step 2 applies with m ≥ 1 and c(y) ≠ 0. So θ′(y) = |c(y)| = (c(y).natAbs : ℝ) is a positive integer, and ξ′(y) = (c(y)/|c(y)|) • simpleNVector σ_1, i.e. ξ′(y) = simpleNVector σ_1 or ξ′(y) = −simpleNVector σ_1.
4. (Representation.) Let ω ∈ Dⁿ(V). The integrand y ↦ Ψ(y)(ω(y)) vanishes on (Y ∖ E) ∖ M′, and E is null. With Y null-measurable, `setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_ae_sdiff_eq_zero` gives S(ω) = ∫_Y Ψ(ω) dHⁿ = ∫_{M′} Ψ(ω) dHⁿ. On M′, θ′(y)·ξ′(y)(ω(y)) = ‖Ψ(y)‖·‖Ψ(y)‖⁻¹·Ψ(y)(ω(y)) = Ψ(y)(ω(y)), since ‖Ψ(y)‖ ≠ 0. Hence S(ω) = ∫_{M′} θ′ ξ′(ω) dHⁿ = tauAction n M′ θ′ ξ′ ω.

 • subset: M′ ⊆ Y ⊆ V.
 • nullMeasurableSet: Y is null-measurable, E is null, and {y ∈ Y : Ψ(y) ≠ 0} = Y ∩ {‖Ψ‖ ≠ 0} is null-measurable, because ‖Ψ‖ is Hⁿ⌞Y-a.e. measurable and Y is null-measurable.

 • pos: θ′(y) = ‖Ψ(y)‖ > 0 for y ∈ M′.
 • integrableOn: for compact K ⊆ V, M′ ∩ K ⊆ Y ∩ K and ‖Ψ‖ is integrable on Y ∩ K (`IntegrableOn.mono_set`).

 • orients: for each k apply (WTC) to (V, M′, θ′, G_k, O_k); its hypotheses are the five items just verified, together with O_k open and G_k C¹ and antilipschitz. Let E′_k be the set of y ∈ M′ ∩ G_k(O_k) for which some w ∈ O_k with G_k(w) = y fails HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M′ θ′ y (range DG_k(w)); E′_k is Hⁿ-null as in Step 1. For y ∈ M′ ∖ ⋃_k E′_k take the family of Step 3. Since y = G_{k_1}(w_1) with w_1 ∈ O_{k_1}, HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M′ θ′ y (range DG_{k_1}(w_1)), and range DG_{k_1}(w_1) = span(range σ_1). Moreover σ_1 is orthonormal and ξ′(y) = ±simpleNVector σ_1 (Step 3), so τ := σ_1 witnesses `orients` at y. This holds for Hⁿ⌞M′-a.e. y.

Conventions: ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) (Lean `Eucl P`) with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|; Hⁿ = μHE[n], Mathlib's Euclidean-normalised n-dimensional Hausdorff measure, which equals Lebesgue measure Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ. An n-covector on E is a continuous alternating n-linear map α : Eⁿ → ℝ with the operator norm. An n-vector is a continuous linear functional on n-covectors (`NVector E n`), also with the operator norm. simpleNVector v is the n-vector α ↦ α(v₁,…,vₙ). For a continuous linear map A, A_#u := nVectorPushforward n A u = u ∘ A^#, where A^#α = α(A·,…,A·). Thus A_# is linear in u, and A_#(simpleNVector v) = simpleNVector(A∘v) (`nVectorPushforward_simple`). `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x T` is Simon's weighted approximate tangent space (Ch. 3, 1.7). By SimonGMT `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique` it is unique when θ(x) ≠ 0, and its first component says dim T = n. The derivative clause for (M, θ, f, L) means: for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x, for every subspace T with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x T and every v ∈ T, the map t ↦ f(x + t v) has derivative L(x)v at t = 0. Φ is c-antilipschitz on Ω if c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω.

This is Steps 4(b), 5, 8 and 9 of the parent proof, stated for an abstract n-vector field Ξ. The parent applies it with Ξ(x) = L(x)_#ξ(x). Two changes from the parent's write-up. First, the image set is taken as Y := {y ∈ V : 1 ≤ N(y) < ∞}, defined by the fibre counting function N; the parent used f(M₊) minus a null set. Second, the density c(y)ζ(y) of the parent is built directly as the fibre sum Ψ(y) = Σ_{x ∈ F_y} θ(x)η_x. Its measurability comes from the fibre-sum measurability in (AF), which the parent's Step 9 also uses, instead of from inverse charts. Throughout, Hⁿ = μHE[n] on ℝ^P and on ℝ^Q, and Σ' is the unordered (tsum) sum.

1. (Positive part.) Put M₊ := {x ∈ M : Ξ(x) ≠ 0} = M ∩ {‖Ξ‖ ≠ 0}. It is Hⁿ-null-measurable. The real function ‖Ξ‖ is Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. measurable, so it agrees with a measurable φ off a set N₀ with Hⁿ⌞M(N₀) = 0; then Hⁿ(N₀ ∩ M) ≤ Hⁿ⌞M(N₀) = 0 (`Measure.le_restrict_apply`). M ∩ {φ ≠ 0} is null-measurable, and its symmetric difference with M₊ lies in the Hⁿ-null set N₀ ∩ M. Since θ(x) ∈ ℕ and θ(x) > 0, θ ≥ 1 on M. subproblem.lean_statement: ((∀ (P n : ℕ) (v : Fin n → Eucl P), ‖simpleNVector v‖ ^ 2 = (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (v i) (v j)).det) ∧ ∀ (P n : ℕ) (B : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (τ : Fin n → Eucl P), simpleNVector (fun i => ∑ j, B i j • τ j) = B.det • simpleNVector τ) → ∀ (P Q n : ℕ) (τ : Fin n → Eucl P) (A : Eucl P →L[ℝ] Eucl Q) (w : NVector (Eucl P) n), Orthonormal ℝ τ → (w = simpleNVector τ ∨ w = -simpleNVector τ) → nVectorPushforward n A w ≠ 0 → LinearIndependent ℝ (fun i => A (τ i)) ∧ ∃ σ : Fin n → Eucl Q, Orthonormal ℝ σ ∧ Submodule.span ℝ (range σ) = Submodule.span ℝ (range (fun i => A (τ i))) ∧ (nVectorPushforward n A w = ‖nVectorPushforward n A w‖ • simpleNVector σ ∨ nVectorPushforward n A w = -(‖nVectorPushforward n A w‖ • simpleNVector σ))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions: ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) (Lean `Eucl P`) with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|; Hⁿ = μHE[n], Mathlib's Euclidean-normalised n-dimensional Hausdorff measure, which equals Lebesgue measure Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ. An n-covector on E is a continuous alternating n-linear map α : Eⁿ → ℝ with the operator norm. An n-vector is a continuous linear functional on n-covectors (`NVector E n`), also with the operator norm. simpleNVector v is the n-vector α ↦ α(v₁,…,vₙ). For a continuous linear map A, A_#u := nVectorPushforward n A u = u ∘ A^#, where A^#α = α(A·,…,A·). Thus A_# is linear in u, and A_#(simpleNVector v) = simpleNVector(A∘v) (`nVectorPushforward_simple`). `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x T` is Simon's weighted approximate tangent space (Ch. 3, 1.7). By SimonGMT `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique` it is unique when θ(x) ≠ 0, and its first component says dim T = n. The derivative clause for (M, θ, f, L) means: for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x, for every subspace T with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x T and every v ∈ T, the map t ↦ f(x + t v) has derivative L(x)v at t = 0. Φ is c-antilipschitz on Ω if c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω.

This is Step 3 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, printed 3.4–3.5) for a single point, with the Gram–Schmidt step made explicit.

1. A_# is linear in its n-vector argument: A_#u = u ∘ A^#, so A_#(−u) = −A_#u (`ContinuousLinearMap.neg_comp`). By `nVectorPushforward_simple`, A_#(simpleNVector τ) = simpleNVector(A∘τ). Hence, with v := A∘τ = (Aτ_1,…,Aτ_n), A_#w = ε • simpleNVector v for some ε ∈ {1, −1}.
2. (i) Suppose v were linearly dependent. Every n-covector α on ℝ^Q is an alternating multilinear map, and alternating multilinear maps vanish on linearly dependent families (`AlternatingMap.map_linearDependent`, applied to α as an alternating map). So α(v) = 0 for every α, i.e. simpleNVector v = 0 (simpleNVector v is the functional α ↦ α(v)). Then A_#w = 0, contradicting the hypothesis. Hence v is linearly independent.
3. Apply Gram–Schmidt to v, indexed by Fin n with its linear order: σ := InnerProductSpace.gramSchmidtNormed ℝ v. It is orthonormal because v is linearly independent (`InnerProductSpace.gramSchmidtNormed_orthonormal`), and span(range σ) = span(range v) (`InnerProductSpace.span_gramSchmidtNormed_range` followed by `InnerProductSpace.span_gramSchmidt`). This is the span assertion of (ii).
4. For each i, v_i ∈ span(range v) = span(range σ), so v_i = Σ_j B_ij σ_j for a real n×n matrix B = (B_ij). By the second conjunct of (SNA), simpleNVector v = det(B) • simpleNVector σ.
5. By part (a) of the sibling lemma lpf_pi_simple_unit_facts (applied to the hypothesis (SNA)), ‖simpleNVector σ‖ = 1. Hence ‖A_#w‖ = ‖ε det(B) • simpleNVector σ‖ = |det B|.
6. By Steps 1 and 4, A_#w = (ε det B) • simpleNVector σ. If ε det B ≥ 0, then ε det B = |det B| = ‖A_#w‖, so A_#w = ‖A_#w‖ • simpleNVector σ. If ε det B < 0, then ε det B = −‖A_#w‖, so A_#w = −(‖A_#w‖ • simpleNVector σ). This completes (ii). For n = 0 every family is empty and B is the empty matrix with det B = 1; the same computation applies. ∎

An n-covector on E is a continuous alternating n-linear map α : Eⁿ → ℝ with the operator norm. An n-vector is a continuous linear functional on n-covectors (`NVector E n`), also with the operator norm. simpleNVector v is the n-vector α ↦ α(v₁,…,vₙ). For a continuous linear map A, A_#u := nVectorPushforward n A u = u ∘ A^#, where A^#α = α(A·,…,A·). Thus A_# is linear in u, and A_#(simpleNVector v) = simpleNVector(A∘v) (`nVectorPushforward_simple`). `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x T` is Simon's weighted approximate tangent space (Ch. 3, 1.7). By SimonGMT `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique` it is unique when θ(x) ≠ 0, and its first component says dim T = n. The derivative clause for (M, θ, f, L) means: for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x, for every subspace T with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x T and every v ∈ T, the map t ↦ f(x + t v) has derivative L(x)v at t = 0. Φ is c-antilipschitz on Ω if c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω.

The parent's disjoint pieces A_{j,k} are replaced by an a.e. statement at the source point x: disjointness, and injectivity of f on the pieces, are not needed for this conclusion. Write Ξ(x) := L(x)_#ξ(x).

1. (Source charts.) The field `countablyRectifiable` says M is countably n-rectifiable, so (CRC) gives C¹ maps Φ_j : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P and open Ω_j ⊆ ℝⁿ with Φ_j K_j-Lipschitz on Ω_j, Φ_j c_j-antilipschitz on Ω_j (c_j > 0), and Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃_j Φ_j(Ω_j)) = 0. Put Ω′_j := Ω_j ∩ Φ_j⁻¹(U), open since Φ_j is continuous and U is open. Φ_j is still K_j-Lipschitz and c_j-antilipschitz on Ω′_j. Since M ⊆ U, M ∩ Φ_j(Ω_j) ⊆ Φ_j(Ω′_j), so Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃_j Φ_j(Ω′_j)) = 0.
